post_title: Scoring Definition Is the Lever in Multi-Agent Deliberation Evals
rationale: The post carries three distinct operator mechanisms that compress into visuals: (1) the 24.0%-57.0% range as a slice-vs-lever diagram for 'What the range actually proves'; (2) the two-route convergence diagram for the abstract's robustness claim in 'The replay, in attributed prose'; and (3) the six-field Scoring Definition Inventory checklist for the operator synthesis section. Three diagrams match the editorial coverage rule (no three consecutive mechanism sections without a visual), distribute the visuals alongside the three strongest claim moments, and avoid a fourth diagram that would crowd the post. All visuals are repo-backed SVG under the post slug, authored against the diagram-style-guide SKILL.md with the current protected-base terminal palette. No generative imagery is used; no inline data: URIs; the standing directive that excludes generative images for berryhill.dev until Matt greenlights that phase is honored.

diagrams.placement_anchor: Insert immediately after the paragraph that ends 'lock the scoring definition first, then read the consensus number'.
diagrams.alt_text: Two stacked horizontal bars compare a single-scoring-definition slice of the consensus number against the full 24.0%-57.0% range produced when the same held-out Wason data is rescored under different scoring definitions.
diagrams.caption: The headline number is a property of the scoring definition that produced it. The 24.0%-57.0% range is the size of the lever, not the size of the agents.

diagrams.placement_anchor: Insert immediately after the paragraph that names the within-0.5 percentage point convergence between the submit-based and participation-matched routes.
diagrams.alt_text: Two complementary post-unblinding routes — submit-based n=98 and participation-matched n=45 — converge within 0.5 percentage points on chat and reasoning mode gaps.
diagrams.caption: The convergence within 0.5pp across the two routes is the strongest evidence the result is robust to scoring-definition choice.

diagrams.placement_anchor: Insert immediately after the closing paragraph that names the six gates and their order of decreasing leverage.
diagrams.alt_text: Six-field Scoring Definition Inventory: participation rule, final-state operationalization, submission-vs-participation alignment, pre-discussion anchoring, chat-vs-reasoning mode, and memorability control, ordered as gates before the consensus number is read.
diagrams.caption: Six gates, one rail. Lock the definition, then read the number — never the reverse.
